prerequisites: Theory of Structures and Industrial Constructions

learning_outcomes.text: Know and predict actions on pipes, as well as design and calculate buried external pipes.
Calculate and design water supply, fire protection, sanitation, and gas transport systems.
Calculate and design piping systems in industrial plants and estimate and minimize the environmental impact of such works.
Calculate, design, and plan ventilation, air conditioning, and fluid treatment systems.
Calculate, design, and plan insulation and noise and vibration control systems.

syllabus_topics: 1.1.- Analysis and design of industrial piping networks.
1.2.- Calculation and sizing of industrial piping networks.
2.4.- Design and calculation of water sanitation networks.
4.1.- Design and calculation of ventilation networks.
Block II: Mechanical Design of Industrial Piping.
6. Components and materials in industrial piping systems.
7. Stresses on piping networks and design codes.
8. Design of piping networks subjected to static and quasi-static loads.
9.1.- Calculation and sizing of industrial pipes subjected to temperature variations.
10. Environmental impact in piping network works.

assessment_methods.method: Block I Exam (Theory and Problem Solving)
Block II Exam (Theory and Problem Solving)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must obtain a minimum score of 5.0 out of 10 in each of the two blocks independently. For the exams of Block I (E1) and Block II (E2), a minimum score of 4.0 is required for the scores from other activities (laboratory practices, classroom activities, and assignments) to be added. If any block score is below 5.0, the final grade will be the minimum between the average of the blocks and 4.0. In extraordinary examinations, a single exam covering both blocks replaces E1 and E2, and previous course activity scores are retained with a 30% weight, subject to the same minimum requirements.
